messages:
ellen-infra: heads up — we've got NIC RX/TX errors and interface flaps on x1d.gpu instances in us-west-2e since the 02:20 deploy. Affected nodes show packet loss east-west and jobs dropping.

tom-sre: noted, can you paste the relevant logs and affected hostnames? is this isolated to x1d or also seen on p4/p3?

ellen-infra: so far only x1d. sample hosts: x1d-3012, x1d-3013, x1d-3020. quick paste from one host: `dmesg | tail -n 20` -> "mlx5_core 0000:af:00.0: NIC Link is Down" and repeated `mlx5e` RX errors.

infra-bot: [ALERT] network-interface-flap on cluster-usw2e (severity: high) — 12 nodes affected, created by ellen-infra at 1753204821

alice-ml: seeing increased model inference tail latency on those hosts, KV cache miss spikes correlate with drops. could be RDMA/verbs falling over.

ben-ops: sharing `ethtool -S ens5` counters from x1d-3012:
```
ethernet: rx_errors: 284
rx_over_errors: 156
tx_aborted_errors: 12
rx_missed_errors: 98
```
Also ran `ethtool -i ens5` -> driver: mlx5_core, firmware: 14.34.1011.

maria-eng: same firmware version across fleet? we pushed a kernel/firmware bundle in the deploy earlier. maybe interaction between new kernel and older NIC firmware.

joan-sre: quick mitigation suggestions: 1) toggle LRO/GRO off (`ethtool -K ens5 gro off lro off`), 2) reduce MTU to 9000->1500 on a canary host, 3) move RDMA traffic off those hosts to fallback pool. propose doing #1 first since it's least disruptive.

ellen-infra: trying `ethtool -K ens5 gro off` on x1d-3012 now. will report.

ben-ops: note: when we toggled GRO on similar issue in eu-central last year it reduced RX overrun but increased CPU. watch for CPU spikes.

ellen-infra: GRO off seems to stabilize RX errors count for ~5m, interface hasn't flapped in last 2 minutes. latency improved slightly.

tom-sre: open a support case with vendor and file internal ticket. include logs, `dmesg`, `ethtool -S`, kernel version, firmware version.

ellen-infra: created internal ticket INFRA-2138 and vendor case VND-9981. attaching snapshot of `dmesg` and `ethtool` output to both.

maria-eng: to reduce blast radius, can we cordon the rest of the x1d pool and drain non-critical jobs? also mark instances with firmware 14.34.1011 as unhealthy for auto-scaler.

joan-sre: yup will add health-check rule to exclude that firmware/driver combo. scheduling a rolling firmware update in maintenance window if vendor confirms fix.

alice-ml: flagging customer-impact — two customers saw degraded throughput, notifying success & account teams.

ben-ops: long-term: consider fleet-wide firmware inventory + automated preflight test (netperf, ib_write_bw) post-deploy.

ellen-infra: thanks all. current plan: keep GRO off on canaries, cordon affected pool, vendor support engaged. I'll post updates here and close once vendor confirms root cause. :thumbsup:
